title: MMTM: Tri-Modal Topic Modeling for Long-Form Video via Similarity-Gated Fusion
task: Topic discovery in long-form video (broadcast news)
problem: Most topic models use text only (or two modalities), ignoring acoustic and visual cues that help segment and interpret video discourse.
architecture: Modular inference-only pipeline: Whisper transcription; audio embeddings (CLAP, Pyannote, MFCC); visual embeddings (OpenCLIP, SigLIP, a VLLM); deterministic similarity-gated fusion of the three modalities; BERTopic clustering of fused segment embeddings, optionally seed-guided; LLM-assisted topic labels (gemma3) for annotators.
llm_or_encoder: Whisper, CLAP, OpenCLIP, SigLIP, gemma3 (labels only)

datasets.name: Tagesschau
datasets.details: German broadcast news, about 54 hours, 1 January - 21 April 2026 (released)

key_results: German: noise 0.273 -> 0.057, transition rate 0.699 -> 0.207, entropy 0.837 -> 0.923 (text-only vs MMTM).
NPMI rises from 0.77 to 0.86 on German but is essentially flat on the shorter NBC broadcasts; visual fusion is the main source of gain.
strengths: Joint use of speech, audio and vision for topic discovery, with a released human-validated corpus.
Each module is replaceable; no training or fine-tuning needed.

limitations.text: Inherits ASR errors; fixed (non-learned) modality weights.
Seed-guided topics may bias discovery toward predefined concepts.
Only two languages and broadcast news; coherence gains are corpus-dependent; no prior tri-modal baseline to compare against.

notes: Code and data promised on acceptance.
